'''Fish and chips''' is a popular dish in England, New Zealand and Australia. The traditional [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] in England is [[Cookbook:Cod|cod]], though this is likely to fall apart or fail to cook in the middle.

==Ingredients==

=== Fish ===
*125 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|plain flour]] 
*125 g (4 oz) [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|corn flour]] (cornstarch)
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
*Enough cold water to form a [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Cod|cod]]/[[Cookbook:Haddock|haddock]]/[[Cookbook:Monkfish|monkfish]] (or any other suitable flaky fish) fillets

=== Chips ===
*4 white [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], Maris Piper preferably
*1 [[Cookbook:Liter|litre]] (1¾ [[Cookbook:Pint|pint]]) [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]] for deep-frying
*Sea salt

=== Serving ===
*1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]], wedged
*Sprig of [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]], to garnish
*Sea salt
*[[Cookbook:Malt vinegar|Malt Vinegar]]
[[Image:Freidora.jpg|thumb|A [[w:deep fryer|deep fryer]] is the safest way to make fish and chips, just as they do at the chipper.]]
==Procedure==
#Preheat the [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]] in a deep fryer to 180°C (350°F), or until a cube of bread browns in 15 seconds when added to the oil.
#Peel the [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]] and cut into thick wedges. [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|Deep-fry]] the potatoes in batches for 6–8 minutes or until they are crisp and golden.
#Remove from the oil, and drain on [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|kitchen paper]]. Sprinkle with sea salt and keep warm.
#In a bowl, whisk together the plain flour, corn flour, salt, and enough cold water to form a [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]].
#Cut the fish into thick slices, then coat in the batter.
#Deep fry the fish in batches for 5–6 minutes, depending on the size of the fish. Remove and drain on kitchen paper.
#Transfer the fish and chips to serving plates and garnish with lemon wedges and sprig of parsley. Or for a fun, traditional twist, place the fried fish and chips on brown paper or newsprint.
#Top with [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] and/or [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]. Typically the lemon wedges are squeezed over the fish and the vinegar is sprinkled on the chips. Also can be served with [[Cookbook:Pickle|pickles]], pickled [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], [[Cookbook:Tartar Sauce|tartar sauce]], pickled [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], and [[Cookbook:Mushy Peas|mushy peas]].

==Warnings==
[[File:Chip-pan-fire.jpg|thumb|[[w:Chip pan|Chip pans]] are extremely dangerous, and are a leading cause of kitchen fires; this demonstrates a simulation of a chip pan fire.]]

* Fish and chips involves [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|deep frying]] and can be dangerous and should only be performed with care. It is a leading cause of house fires in England, and further, may spill hot oil, causing severe burns.
